_note: Every place under src/ where a Step orders, or bans, a second lookup. The stall rule in core/guardrails.md enumerates the only repeats that stay allowed, and each site here says which claim it makes — so dropping an exemption from the rule reddens the sites that leaned on it, and a new repeat has to be argued for here instead of appended to the rule as one more clause. `claim`: the CAPS word the rule exempts (`changed`, `written`), `forbidden` where the site bans the repeat, `not-a-repeat` where the run does not already hold the material. A sha covers the matched phrase plus 45 characters either side; edit a site and the suite prints the new entry to paste.

sites.reason: Printed text asking the USER to invoke the command again after a force-push. A fresh invocation fetches everything from scratch; nothing is being re-read inside one run.
Names re-fetching the diff and re-listing comments as the workarounds a failed post must not try.
A second `git worktree add` for the same submodule is banned; the first one already produced the tree.
The submodule's head is the one Step C already read — re-fetching it here would anchor findings to a tree no Step reviewed.
Printed text asking the USER to check out the right branch and invoke the command again.
The matching pass is bounded to the Context already fetched; re-reading the marker rules or re-running the fetch is the loop the stall rule exists for.
A finding the dev already decided on is skipped; asking a second time is the question-shaped form of the same stall.
`.gitmodules` is read once per run, and no earlier Step holds it. `never cached` bans trusting a PREVIOUS run's conclusion — settings carry no submodule field precisely so this read decides it.
The head is fetched a second time to learn whether it MOVED while the review ran. The first value cannot answer that.
Once the check above resolves `<commit_id>`, the overview and the payload reuse it; a third fetch would answer what the second already did.
`.review-skipped.md` is written by an earlier Step of this same run, so what is in context predates the file's final contents.
The vendor is already parsed by the caller; deriving it again, or asking the user for it, repeats work whose answer is in context.
Describes what a LATER review does with a REFERENCE line: it reads the pointed-at path then, instead of memory holding a copy. No lookup is repeated inside the doctor run.
Import just copied this repo's settings.json into <data>; the first settings call read defaults from a file that did not exist yet, so the second reads what the copy WROTE.
